text:
A: Hello! Yeah, there he is. Can you hear me, uncle? Sorry, sorry, can I call you uncle? Your photo, you look like proper uncle.
B: Ha! Yes, yes, call me what you like. Abdul. Everybody at work calls me uncle anyway, even the doctors.
A: Hitesh. Peterborough. Where you are?
B: Leyton, East London. Thirty years I'm in East London. You're in Peterborough, very nice. What you do there?
A: Factory, chilled food, I'm on flow-wrap machine. Basically I'm the guy who knows how to fix it when it jams, you know, supervisor comes to me. Part-time, but that's my choice, yeah, because I do delivery also, and my own business ideas, so.
B: Business ideas! Good, good. What kind of business?
A: Er, phones, maybe. I used to work in my cousin's phone shop back home, Gujarat, I can unlock anything, fix screen, anything. Or taxi licence. Or, you know, investments.
B: Investments, ah. Shares and all that?
A: Bit of crypto, bit of shares. Some up, some down, that's the game, innit. You have to be in it.
B: Me, I don't understand it. My money goes in the bank and then to my sister's kids for school. That's my investment.
A: That's also good, mate. Safe. What's your job?
B: Hospital porter, Whitechapel. Sixteen years. Pushing beds, wheelchairs, oxygen, everything. Twenty thousand steps a shift, my shoes finished every few months.
A: Twenty thousand! You don't need gym then.
B: No gym. The hospital is my gym. You play any sport?
A: Cricket, mate. Sunday, tape-ball, in the park, with the guys. Mostly for the banter, but I'm good, I bowl fast. And IPL, every match. Mumbai Indians.
B: Mumbai! Ah. I play tape-ball also, Victoria Park, until my knees said no. Now I umpire. And I'm Bangladesh, of course.
A: Bangladesh, oh no. Sorry, uncle. Last week, that match...
B: Don't. I was talking about this one already today with the gentleman before, Nilesh. Three wickets in two overs. I am still not sleeping properly.
A: Ha! At least they lost properly. Mumbai, last night, our guy drops simple catch. Simple! My son Dev could catch that, and he's twelve. I was shouting at the TV, my wife says the neighbours will complain.
B: The umpire in me says it's a hard catch maybe. The fan in me says, no, he should catch.
A: No, no, uncle, no hard catch. Straight in the hands. I was saying to my brother on WhatsApp, this guy should be dropped himself. Big argument in the family group now.
B: Family group, yes, we have one too, everybody in Sylhet, everybody in London, all shouting. You have big family here?
A: Brother in Leicester. He has shop there. Doing well, you know, he's... yeah, he's doing well. Parents are in India still. My father, er, his health is not so great now.
B: Ah. I'm sorry to hear. You go back often?
A: Every two, three years, for the weddings mostly. Should be more. But tickets, holidays, work, you know how it is.
B: I know. I know exactly. Me also, I save one month leave, then go. It's never enough. Call him a lot, that's what I say. Phone is free now.
A: Yeah. Yeah, I do. My wife says I talk more to the cricket than to my dad, but... anyway. Sorry, sorry, what was the question? I'm going everywhere.
B: No question! We are just chatting, it's fine. Tell me, the puzzle at the start, you finished it?
A: Puzzle, honestly, mate, waste of time. I did the first two fast, then the last one, I thought, who is checking? I just clicked something.
B: Ha! Same as Nilesh, he's guessing also. I think nobody finished, only the researchers.
A: They make it, so they know the answer, innit. Easy for them. Like my supervisor, he makes the rules, then he—
